To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new image processing method to detect the moving objects and enhance the contrast and edges of the scene.
the proposed method enhances the motion and edges in the image and suppresses other features, resulting in an activity matrix with higher resolution and better quality than other techniques.
the proposed image processing method outperforms other methods in terms of image quality and perceived image.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an image processing algorithm that can improve the perception of images by visual prosthesis users.
improving the perception of the prosthetic vision using a new image processing method that enhances three main features detectible by the visual pathway.
improving the quality and resolution of the perceived image by the blind through the enhancement of three features detectable by natural visual pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a better choice than the other techniques to generate the electric stimulus for the electrodes array in the thalamic visual prosthesis.
the proposed method is the best method in the context of visual prostheses, and it is the only method that can be used to generate the activity matrix for the electrodes array.
the proposed method is the most suitable one for the visual prosthesis application in terms of the image quality and the resolution of the resulting perceived image.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed an image processing method for visual prostheses that enhances the contrast, motion, edges and reduces the size of image to be displayed on the electrodes array.
the proposed method can improve the resolution of prosthetic images by enhancing the contrast, motion and edges in the scene.
we are trying to enhance the quality of the perceived images for the blind using image processing techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of the image and the perception are highly related and that the proposed method can be used to enhance the quality of the perceived image.

by using the proposed method, the number of electrodes needed to achieve a specific resolution can be reduced by 40% which is an important step toward the development of high resolution thalamic visual prosthesis.
the proposed image processing technique can be used as a preprocessing step in visual prosthetic applications to enhance the quality of the visual perception.
